description: Compare each team's home-game total with the average of all teams' totals.

a.request: For each team (`team_id`) in `home_game`, add up its home `games`, ignoring missing values. Return the team id, that total, the total as a fraction of the sum over all teams, and the total divided by the average of these team totals across all teams. Sort by that last ratio from highest to lowest (missing last), keep the top 10, and don't round.
a.sql: WITH team_totals AS (SELECT team_id, SUM(games) AS total_games FROM home_game GROUP BY team_id), totals AS (SELECT SUM(total_games) AS all_games, AVG(total_games) AS avg_team_games FROM team_totals) SELECT t.team_id, t.total_games, 1.0 * t.total_games / totals.all_games AS fraction_of_all_games, t.total_games / totals.avg_team_games AS ratio_to_avg_team_games FROM team_totals AS t CROSS JOIN totals ORDER BY ratio_to_avg_team_games IS NULL, ratio_to_avg_team_games DESC LIMIT 10

b.request: For each team ID, sum its nonmissing home-game counts, divide that total by the average of those totals across all teams, and report its share of the grand total of home games; return the 10 highest ratios in descending order, with missing ratios last and no rounding
b.sql: WITH team_totals AS (SELECT team_id, SUM(games) AS total_home_games FROM home_game GROUP BY team_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(total_home_games) AS average_home_games, SUM(total_home_games) AS grand_total_home_games FROM team_totals), results AS (SELECT t.team_id, t.total_home_games, 1.0 * t.total_home_games / NULLIF(o.average_home_games, 0) AS ratio, 1.0 * t.total_home_games / NULLIF(o.grand_total_home_games, 0) AS share_of_grand_total FROM team_totals AS t CROSS JOIN overall AS o) SELECT * FROM results ORDER BY ratio IS NULL, ratio DESC LIMIT 10;

c.request: Which 10 teams have the most home games relative to the average? For each team id, give its total home games (ignoring missing values), its share of all home games, and its total divided by the average number of home games. Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest (missing last) and don't round. Compare each team's home-game total with the average of all teams' totals.
c.sql: WITH team_totals AS (SELECT team_id, SUM(ghome) AS total_home_games FROM team WHERE team_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY team_id), averages AS (SELECT AVG(total_home_games) AS avg_home_games, SUM(total_home_games) AS all_home_games FROM team_totals) SELECT t.team_id, t.total_home_games, 1.0 * t.total_home_games / a.all_home_games AS share_of_all_home_games, 1.0 * t.total_home_games / a.avg_home_games AS ratio_to_average FROM team_totals AS t CROSS JOIN averages AS a ORDER BY ratio_to_average IS NULL, ratio_to_average DESC LIMIT 10;

d.request: Which 10 teams have the highest home-game totals relative to the average total across all teams? For each team ID, report its total home games (ignoring missing values), its share of all home games, and its total divided by the average team total. Sort by that ratio from highest to lowest, put missing values last, and do not round.
d.sql: WITH team_totals AS (SELECT team_id, SUM(ghome) AS total_home_games FROM team GROUP BY team_id), overall AS (SELECT SUM(total_home_games) AS all_home_games, AVG(total_home_games) AS average_team_total FROM team_totals) SELECT t.team_id, t.total_home_games, t.total_home_games * 1.0 / o.all_home_games AS share_of_all_home_games, t.total_home_games / o.average_team_total AS ratio_to_average FROM team_totals AS t CROSS JOIN overall AS o ORDER BY ratio_to_average DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
